runs.text: Explain the JavaScript event loop.

beats.say: When code runs, async work is handed to the browser's Web APIs.
When that work finishes, its callback waits in the task queue.
The event loop watches both the stack and the queue.
When the stack is empty, it pushes the next queued task onto it.
So callbacks never interrupt running code; they wait their turn.

runs.text: Show me how binary search works.

beats.say: Binary search starts with a sorted array and checks the middle element.
We compare that middle value to the target.
If they match, we're done — found it.
If the target is smaller, discard the right and search the left half.
If it's larger, search the right half instead.
Each step halves the search space, so lookups stay fast.

runs.text: Explain Big O notation with examples.

Linear time, O of n, grows in direct proportion to input size.
Quadratic time, O of n squared, grows much faster as input grows.
For example, searching a list is often O of n, while some sorting algorithms are O of n squared.
Lower complexity scales well; higher complexity slows down quickly as data grows.

runs.text: How does inserting into a linked list work?

beats.say: A linked list has nodes connected by pointers. Each node stores data and a reference to the next node.
To insert, create a new node and set its next pointer to the node currently in front of it.
If inserting at the head, the new node's next points to the old head.
If inserting in the middle, its next points to the following node. Nobody shifts like an array.
So insertion is just rewiring pointers, not moving the whole list.

If unvisited nodes remain, loop back and pick again.
Once all nodes are visited, every shortest path is found.

runs.text: Explain the CAP theorem.

beats.say: The CAP theorem describes three guarantees a distributed data store can want.
Consistency means every read sees the latest write. Availability means every request gets a response. Partition tolerance means the system keeps working despite dropped messages.
When a network partition happens, you must trade off consistency against availability. CA systems skip partition tolerance, CP systems favor consistency, and AP systems favor availability.
